slides.eyebrow: If you only remember one thing:
slides.sub: 6 years in real estate taught me to check these 4 first.

slides.title: Who gave it
slides.body: On a Fannie Mae loan, the gift can come from a relative, a fiancé, a domestic partner or someone with a long-standing family-like bond. FHA has its own donor list. Ask your lender.

slides.title: The gift letter
slides.body: The donor signs it. It lists the gift amount, the donor's name, address, phone number and relationship to you, and says you don't have to pay it back.

slides.title: How the money moved
slides.body: Lenders want to see the transfer. For example: the donor's check and your deposit slip, or a transfer straight to the closing agent.

slides.label: LARGE DEPOSIT
slides.body: On a Fannie Mae purchase loan, a single deposit over 50% of your monthly qualifying income may need proof of where it came from. Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.

caption:
If you only remember one thing about gift money for your down payment: it may not count without a paper trail.
